definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.110) interface of an object lists the methods with their parameters, returned value and exceptions, word for word 2023 3.109 apart from 'may'/'can'; the rule names an interface as the language construct (§2002:4 4.111 'A grouping of method prototypes'), defined alike in 2023 3.110, so scope is unchanged. SR5's 'this interface conforms' uses the construct and the conformance relation of §2002:9.3.7.1.2, which the reader compared item by item.

definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 (4.121) method 'A procedural entity defined by a method definition within, or inherited by, a class definition' names the same entity 2023 describes in 9.3.4; the method definitions the rule places or refuses are the same source elements.

pending-clause.answer: Read §2002:9.3.5 (binding by name, no overloading in 2002). SR5 concerns a method-name inherited from several interfaces and their conformance (§2002:9.3.7.1.2), not the binding of an invocation; with one prototype per name the requirement is the same, and the 2002 runs (COBOL2762 refusal, MATCH legal) show it.
